item.title: Why Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang: All you need to know
item.description: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang will remain in his role as the company's board investigates reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation ...
item.dc:creator: Barkha Mathur
item.content:encoded: US chipmaker Nvidia has launched an independent investigation following reports that its founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, the company's board of directors said in a statement on Sunday. The announcement follows reports by various publications that a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, allegedly developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang while gathering information for Beijing. The board, however, has said it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information was compromised. What exactly happened? The New York Times reported on Saturday that China's Ministry of State Security had recruited Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman, to gather intelligence on Jensen Huang. According to the report, a memo circulated among senior policymakers in the Trump administration last spring cited intelligence that Alice Huang was working for China's top intelligence agency. The alleged objective was to obtain information about Nvidia and its CEO, including potentially influencing the company to support making its most advanced AI chips available to China. Alice Huang was associated with Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has been a significant Nvidia customer. The New York Times reported that Megaspeed had purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the preceding two years. The reports also alleged that Jensen Huang had developed a close, personal relationship with Alice Huang. He subsequently acknowledged in a message to Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues. Why has Nvidia's board ordered an investigation? The board announced that it was initiating an independent investigation in light of the reporting. A committee of independent directors, assisted by external independent legal counsel, will oversee the inquiry. The board has made three points clear:It considers US national and economic security paramount to Nvidia and its shareholders.It has no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised.Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating fully.The board has also reiterated its confidence in Huang and his leadership team. He is expected to continue leading Nvidia while the inquiry proceeds. Why Chinese connection particularly sensitive? The US government has imposed export restrictions to prevent China from accessing the most advanced American semiconductor technology. The restrictions are intended to limit China's ability to develop advanced AI and other strategic technologies with potential military applications. The New York Times reported that the alleged intelligence operation was intended not just to gather information but potentially to influence Nvidia's position on chip exports to China. Megaspeed's business relationship with Nvidia is also relevant because US authorities have reportedly scrutinised the company over suspicions that it helped Beijing obtain advanced chips restricted from export to China. The allegations have also gained political attention and three Republican committee chairs in the US House of Representatives asked Huang to brief Congress on his interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia's safeguards for protecting sensitive information. They said the reports raised national security concerns about China's potential access to sensitive US technology and information. They sought a response by November 11. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had not discussed the allegations with Huang, but described him as an honourable person and praised his contribution to Nvidia. ALSO READ: What Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in email as board launches probe Why is Nvidia valuable? Nvidia sits at the centre of the US-China technology rivalry. Its advanced graphics processing units (GPUs) are essential for training and running sophisticated AI models. Its CUDA software platform allows developers to build and run applications on Nvidia GPUs. Thus, the company has become one of the most important suppliers of the infrastructure powering the global AI industry. Nvidia's latest reported quarterly results show that data centre operations accounted for the overwhelming bulk ($89 billion) of its quarterly revenue ($96.2 billion). For the full fiscal year 2026, Nvidia reported revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65 per cent from the previous year. Nvidia has become the world's second-most valuable publicly listed company after Apple, with a market capitalisation of approximately $4.5 trillion. But its stock has beein experiencing considerable volatility in recent weeks. As of November 6, Nvidia shares closed at approximately $186.64. The stock had fallen for five consecutive weeks and was around 22 per cent below its October 6 record closing level. The decline had wiped out approximately $1.27 trillion in market value from its peak. ALSO READ: Nvidia CEO Huang admits affair with Chinese spy, company launches probe The investigation introduces another source of uncertainty for a stock already facing pressure from concerns about the sustainability of AI spending. Reuters quoted Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co as saying that the investigation could create risks for the stock because of Huang's importance to Nvidia's global strategy. However, the market reaction is yet to be seen as the board's announcement came after the US market had closed on Friday.

item.title: Consumer firms absorb rising costs as inflation squeezes household budgets
item.description: India’s consumer giants are increasingly absorbing higher costs from surging inflation rather than passing them on to financially stretched consumers, a sign that weakening household purchasing power ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Satviki Sanjay and Ruchi Bhatia India’s consumer giants are increasingly absorbing higher costs from surging inflation rather than passing them on to financially stretched consumers, a sign that weakening household purchasing power is beginning to squeeze corporate margins. Westlife Foodworld Ltd., the operator of McDonald’s Corp.’s fast food chain stores in western and southern India, is “quite conservative” about raising prices beyond its standard annual hike to keep store traffic strong, its Chief Executive Officer Akshay Jatia told Bloomberg News. “We need to make sure that we don’t shoot ourselves in the foot over there.” Westlife is among at least 15 consumer-facing companies cautious on raising prices or holding the line, with firms such as KFC and Pizza Hut operators Devyani International Ltd. and Sapphire Foods India Ltd., leading paint maker Asian Paints Ltd., and retailer V-Mart Retail Ltd. all flagging concerns about an uneven demand outlook as a reason. India’s inflation accelerated to an almost two-year high of 5.54% in September, driven largely by food costs. Food inflation jumped to 7.74%, with prices rising sharply across vegetables, fruits, edible oils, sugar and prepared foods. Pricing pressure is also spreading beyond groceries, with costs for transport, restaurants and other services picking up, adding to the squeeze on household budgets. “With monetary and credit conditions tightening substantially, discretionary consumption is likely to moderate over the next few quarters,” Suvodeep Rakshit, an economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, said in an interview. That has made many consumer brands wary that further price increases could chip away at sales growth. As a result, some of these companies that are putting off price hikes, such as PepsiCo’s India bottler Varun Beverages Ltd., are warning about lower margins. “There is margin pressure due to raw material price,” Varun Jaipuria, the company’s executive vice chair, told analysts on an Oct. 30 conference call. “Everybody is under pressure, they’re figuring out what to do and how do you negate the cost.” For liquor maker United Spirits, a unit of Diageo Plc in India, higher costs of living has started to hit lower-income consumers and have hurt its portfolio of entry-level spirits, Praveen Someshwar, its chief executive officer, said on an earnings call last month. “The bottom end of the urban consumer is feeling the inflationary pressure,” he said. That challenge extends to food products including snacks, with analysts at brokerages such as Motilal Oswal warning in a report published on Oct. 15 of the risk of higher commodity costs weighing on Nestle India Ltd. Indian consumption growth is expected to slow to 3.5% in the current quarter, compared with 5.2% in the three months to June 30, according to data from Worldpanel by Numerator. “We are seeing a kind of short-term stress on the budget,” Manoj Menon, the Mumbai-based director for commercial at the market research firm, said in an interview.  The signals on consumption are mixed. Tax collections and digital spending in India remain strong, suggesting consumers are still spending for now, even as surveys point to growing strain beneath the surface. HSBC Holdings Plc’s gauge of 100 growth indicators showed the breadth of economic expansion narrowing in September. Domestic activity is likely to soften after December as elevated costs erode consumers’ purchasing power, according to a note by HSBC economist Aayushi Chaudhary. She expects growth to moderate in the second half of fiscal 2027, amid weaker demand from the informal sector, rising costs and tighter financial conditions. To avoid hurting demand, consumer-goods maker Devyani is offering more products at entry-level price points, Manish Dawar, its group chief executive officer, told analysts in a post-earnings call on Nov. 2. “With food inflation firming and interest rates beginning to rise, we expect discretionary spending to stay under pressure,” he said.  Instead of raising prices across the board, Nestle India is focusing on “operational efficiencies” to cushion its bottom line from higher costs, the company said last month when it reported second-quarter results. The caution follows price increases by Nestle and other big consumer companies earlier in the year after commodity costs surged amid the Middle East conflict. For now, the annual festival season may provide a buffer, with demand for staples expected to remain resilient as spending builds toward Diwali in November. This period usually sees strong spending patterns and historically has accounted for nearly a third of annual sales for many consumer companies.  Still, the disconnect between headline growth of around 7% and “what households and businesses are experiencing on the ground raises concerns about the strength of the consumption outlook,” Shumita Deveshwar, an economist at TS Lombard, said in an interview. “The big question is how much of the cost burden companies can absorb before it starts weighing on demand.”

Asian stocks steady as AI, West Asia jitters ease; dollar firms on Fed bets MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.8% after sliding 4.6% last week. Japan's Nikkei index added 2.5% while Korean shares made small gains

Taiwan's benchmark rose about 2.5% after notching its heaviest weekly drop for two decades last week, when fears about AI profitability and infrastructure demand turned into a rout following wins by Democrats at US midterm polls | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters HONG KONG 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 7:51 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Asian markets and US equity futures made a steady start on Monday, wobbling into positive territory after a wild week where doubts about demand for computer chips sent tech-heavy markets in Asia into some of their steepest falls in years. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.8% after sliding 4.6% last week. Japan's Nikkei index added 2.5% while Korean shares made small gains. Taiwan's benchmark rose about 2.5% after notching its heaviest weekly drop for two decades last week, when fears about AI profitability and infrastructure demand turned into a rout following wins by Democrats at US midterm polls.

US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, were a touch higher. On Friday, Wall Street equities rallied to end a chaotic week after heavy AI-related selling, helping to calm some nerves. Global stocks had already been on shaky ground in recent weeks with the AI trade crumbling in the face of rising interest rates, until the US midterm results unleashed deeper worries about increased regulation of AI and data centres. Stock Market Close: Sensex surges 2,009 pts, Nifty ends at 24,537; investors add ₹7 trn to wealth

What Asian stock investors need to watch ahead of US midterm elections

Earnings reports due this week from tech companies including CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are set to put the profitability of AI ambitions to the test amid the massive costs of the build-out.

Meanwhile, a company-led investigation by industry bellwether Nvidia into its CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy could also draw some volatility. "The markets are far from being out of the woods yet," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. "Following last week's midterm elections that have led to increased regulatory risk and an overall underwhelming earnings season that's seen Magnificent Seven companies miss earnings expectations, the momentum remains skewed to the downside," he added. Elsewhere, Brent crude fell to $97.49 per barrel after US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress.

FED HIKE BETS BUILD A blowout jobs report on Friday showed US employers added 165,000 jobs last month, more than twice economists' expectations and bolstering the case for the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in December. A US CPI reading due on Tuesday could further cement expectations for a hike next month. Market expectations for an increase of at least 25 basis points at the central bank's December meeting moved up to nearly 80% in the wake of the report, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Comments from officials also supported views for a rate hike, with New York Fed President John Williams saying US economic growth has remained remarkably resilient in the face of successive shocks but inflation is too high and it is essential to bring it back to 2%.

That helped the greenback to notch its biggest single-day gain in five months. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, last traded at 102.2. The European single currency was little changed at $1.1148. The yen was 0.2% stronger at 158.215. Bitcoin fell by more than 2% to $73,708, while ether fell about 5% to $2,223, touching the lowest levels in over two months as investors fretted a Democratic-controlled US Congress will toughen regulation on cryptocurrencies.
